claims.text: For the meaning of his name refer to Túrin - Etymology. Túrin I was probably named after Túrin Turambar, a tragic hero of the Edain of the First Age.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Carl F. Hostetter (ed.), "Part Two. Body, Mind and Spirit: V. Beards", The Nature of Middle-earth, HarperCollins, 2021, footnote 3, p. 189; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Peoples of Middle-earth, "VII. The Heirs of Elendil", p. 203

claims.text: Túrin's stewardship occurred during the period of the Watchful Peace (-).
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix B, "The Third Age"

claims.text: Túrin ruled as Steward for thirty-four years. Very unusually for a noble of Gondor, he married twice and had several daughters. Only his last child, born in his old age, was a son, Hador by whom he was succeeded.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Peoples of Middle-earth, "VII. The Heirs of Elendil", p. 204; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A, "The Númenorean Kings", "The Realms in Exile", "The Southern Line: Heirs of Anarion"
